question: Which condition is a major driver of high-risk admissions in Nigerian maternity units?
explanation: Severe pre-eclampsia is one of the leading causes of high-risk admissions and maternal complications in local clinical settings. [learn more](BMP313_U1_T3#BMP313_U1_T3_h1)

question: Why is recognizing a creeping pulse so vital in maternity care?

options.A: It helps midwives catch early red flags before a crisis deepens
options.B: It proves the patient is ready for discharge
options.C: It confirms the baby is in the second stage of labor
options.D: It replaces the need for blood pressure checks

explanation: Subtle changes in vital signs often point toward hidden deterioration, allowing the team to intervene before shock sets in. [learn more](BMP313_U1_T3#BMP313_U1_T3_h1)

question: Who is typically included in a multidisciplinary review panel?
explanation: A complete panel requires clinical input from all major specialties involved in direct patient care during an emergency. [learn more](BMP313_U1_T3#BMP313_U1_T3_h2)

question: What is the primary goal of holding a case review after a critical incident?

options.A: Issuing immediate dismissal letters to staff members involved
options.B: Conducting an objective breakdown of the event without personal blame
options.C: Fulfilling a basic paperwork requirement for government archiving
options.D: Proving that midwives are solely responsible for negative outcomes

explanation: Blame-free reviews encourage honest participation and focus on system fixes rather than personal fault. [learn more](BMP313_U1_T3#BMP313_U1_T3_h2)

question: Why is the bedside midwife's perspective so valuable during a clinical case review?

options.A: They purchase medical supplies from external vendors
options.B: They write the final legal verdicts for the medical board
options.C: They provide the exact timeline of bedside events and interventions
options.D: They handle all hospital financial accounting and budget planning

explanation: The bedside midwife tracks real-time changes and intervention timings better than anyone else on the healthcare team. [learn more](BMP313_U1_T3#BMP313_U1_T3_h3)

question: How should a midwife approach systemic hurdles like blood shortages during a panel discussion?

options.A: Bring them to the center of discussion to seek structural solutions
options.B: Hide them to protect the reputation of the maternity ward
options.C: Blame individual patients for failing to bring blood donors
options.D: Assume they have no impact on overall maternal survival rates

explanation: Highlighting systemic barriers helps the wider management team address root causes rather than just treating symptoms. [learn more](BMP313_U1_T3#BMP313_U1_T3_h3)

question: What best describes a maternal near-miss event?

options.A: A woman who nearly died from a complication but survived
options.B: A normal delivery with zero blood loss or perineal tears
options.C: An elective cesarean section performed without any anesthesia
options.D: A routine antenatal clinic visit with no clinical complaints

explanation: Survival after facing a life-threatening obstetric complication is the core definition of a near-miss. [learn more](BMP313_U1_T3#BMP313_U1_T3_h4)

question: Why do clinical teams place high value on reviewing near-miss cases alongside actual deaths?

options.A: Near-misses require zero paperwork compared to maternal deaths
options.B: Near-misses provide rich safety data without the finality of a tragedy
options.C: Families never complain about care when a near-miss occurs
options.D: Government agencies only provide funding for near-miss audits

explanation: Studying cases where patients survived yields vital lessons on what worked well and where systems nearly collapsed. [learn more](BMP313_U1_T3#BMP313_U1_T3_h4)

question: Which medication is standard practice for managing severe pre-eclampsia?
explanation: Magnesium sulfate is the recognized drug of choice for preventing and treating eclamptic seizures. [learn more](BMP313_U1_T3#BMP313_U1_T3_h5)

question: A panel discovers a midwife used an outdated practice during a postpartum hemorrhage. What is the most constructive response?

options.A: Suspend all midwives working in the maternity unit indefinitely
options.B: Update team training on current evidence-based hemorrhage guidelines
options.C: Ignore the finding since the patient eventually recovered
options.D: Tell the staff to rely solely on personal intuition in future emergencies

explanation: Uncovering outdated practices should always trigger educational updates and protocol alignment across the unit. [learn more](BMP313_U1_T3#BMP313_U1_T3_h5)

question: What is a critical final step following a multidisciplinary case review session?

options.A: Turning panel lessons into practical, facility-wide protocol changes
options.B: Punishing staff members who made minor documentation errors
options.C: Stopping all future audits to save staff working hours
options.D: Archiving all review notes in a locked cabinet permanently

explanation: Actionable changes bridge the gap between identifying past mistakes and preventing future harm. [learn more](BMP313_U1_T3#BMP313_U1_T3_h6)

question: Why are regular emergency drills important after identifying a protocol gap during a case review?

options.A: They allow the hospital to pass external financial audits easily
options.B: They build team muscle memory and ensure staff can execute new protocols smoothly
options.C: They replace the need for maintaining adequate drug supplies on the ward
options.D: They serve as punishment for midwives who fail clinical examinations

explanation: Drills bridge the gap between reading a protocol on paper and performing it calmly under real-world pressure. [learn more](BMP313_U1_T3#BMP313_U1_T3_h6)
